Determiners (articles, this/these, a few, a little, each)

questions.rule: Everyone is singular, so it takes a singular verb: makes.

options: Hawking was diagnosed with ALS at the age of 21.
Hawking was diagnose with ALS at the age of 21.
Hawking diagnosed with ALS at the age of 21.
questions.rule: Passive = was + past participle: was diagnosed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Before a noun, use the possessive determiner: his voice.

chat: Have you seen the film about Stephen Hawking?
options: Yes, I have seen it twice.
Yes, I have saw it twice.
questions.rule: Present perfect = have + past participle: have seen.

questions.source: Hawking wrote A Brief History of Time.
options: A Brief History of Time is written by Hawking.
A Brief History of Time was written by Hawking.
A Brief History of Time was wrote by Hawking.
questions.rule: Simple past active becomes was + past participle: was written.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Two subjects joined by and take a plural verb (want). Every one of takes a singular verb (has).

options: Hawking had a few close friends who visited him often.
Hawking had a little close friends who visited him often.
Hawking had few a close friends who visited him often.
questions.rule: A few goes with countable plural nouns (friends); 'a little' is for uncountable nouns.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
questions.rule: A finished past time (in 1988) takes the simple past, not the present perfect.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Passive needs the past participle: was taken (take - took - taken).

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: News looks plural but is uncountable and singular: the news was.
Since + a point in time goes with the present perfect: has sold.
The book does not translate; people translate it. Passive: has been + past participle.
A few goes with countable plural nouns (events); his comes before 'whole life'.

chat: Who is coming to the planetarium?
options: Neither Asha nor her sisters is coming.
Neither Asha nor her sisters am coming.
Neither Asha nor her sisters are coming.
questions.rule: With neither ... nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject: sisters are.

options: It was shoot in Cambridge, I think.
It was shot in Cambridge, I think.
It is shot in Cambridge, I think.
questions.rule: Past passive: was + past participle (shot). The question is in the past, so not 'is'.

questions.prompt: Make a wh-question asking about the number of books.
options: How many books Hawking has written?
How many books has Hawking written?
How many books has Hawking wrote?
questions.rule: Question order: How many books + has + subject + past participle?

options: Ten kilometres are a long distance to walk.
Ten kilometre is a long distance to walk.
Ten kilometres is a long distance to walk.
questions.rule: A distance, amount or sum taken as one whole takes a singular verb: ten kilometres is.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: He has been rushed to the hospital last April.
He was rushed to the hospital last April.
He was rush to the hospital last April.
questions.rule: Last April is a finished time: simple past passive was rushed.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: With uncountable nouns like time, say very little, not 'very less'.

questions.before: Neither the doctors nor the nurse
questions.after: sure about his illness at first.
questions.rule: Neither ... nor: the verb agrees with the nearer subject (the nurse): was.

questions.after: at a medical clinic for two weeks in 1963.
questions.rule: In 1963 is a finished past time, so use the simple past: stayed.
Present perfect passive: has been + past participle (+ by ...).

chat: Do you have any books on black holes?
options: Yes, I have a little. You can borrow one.
Yes, I have much. You can borrow one.
Yes, I have a few. You can borrow one.
questions.rule: Books are countable, so use a few. 'A little' and 'much' are for uncountable nouns.

chat: When did you finish A Brief History of Time?
options: I have finished it last week.
I have finish it last week.
questions.rule: When ...? and last week need the simple past: I finished.

questions.source: A computer programmer developed a speaking program.
options: A speaking program was developed by a computer programmer.
A speaking program developed by a computer programmer.
A speaking program was develop by a computer programmer.
questions.rule: Simple past passive: object + was + past participle + by + doer.

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Millions of people is plural: have read. Neither of us takes a singular verb: has.

options: Either of the two answers are correct.
Either of the two answers is correct.
Either of the two answer is correct.
questions.rule: Either of + plural noun takes a singular verb: either of the two answers is.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: three books is plural, so use the plural determiner these, not 'this'.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Present perfect + a point in time (2019) uses since; 'for' goes with a period (for six years).

questions.after: by students all over the world.
questions.rule: Ideas don't study; students study them. Present passive: are + past participle.
Neither ... nor: the verb agrees with the nearer subject, doctors, so use were.

chat: Has the science project been submitted?
options: Yes, ma'am. It was submitted yesterday.
Yes, ma'am. It was submit yesterday.
questions.rule: The project was handed in by someone: past passive was submitted with 'yesterday'.

chat: How much time do we have before the quiz?
options: We have very little time, so let's hurry.
We have very few time, so let's hurry.
We have very less times, so let's hurry.
questions.rule: Time is uncountable, so use little; 'few' is for countable nouns.

questions.prompt: Change into a negative sentence without changing the meaning.
options: Riya has not never been late.
questions.rule: Use never + the opposite word: always punctual = never late. Avoid double negatives.

questions.source: Did the doctors take a muscle sample?
options: Did a muscle sample taken by the doctors?
Was a muscle sample took by the doctors?
Was a muscle sample taken by the doctors?
questions.rule: A Did ...? question becomes Was/Were + object + past participle ...?

questions.prompt: Find and fix the 2 errors in this message.
questions.rule: Each of takes a singular verb (explains); a few of them is plural (have).

options: Hawking, along with his students, was working on black holes.
Hawking, along with his students, were working on black holes.
Hawking, along with his students, are working on black holes.
questions.rule: along with ... does not change the subject. Hawking is singular: was.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.
questions.rule: Both verbs share were: were selected ... and then passed (past participle).

questions.after: of the two scientists has won the award.
questions.rule: Neither of takes a singular verb (has). 'Both' needs 'have'; 'all' is for more than two.
Present perfect question: Have + you + ever + past participle ...?

chat: The principal has finally approved our space club.
options: Great! Everyone in our class is excited.
Great! Everyone in our class are excited.
Great! Everyone in our class were excited.
questions.rule: Everyone is singular: everyone is, even when followed by 'in our class'.

questions.source: The doctors gave him two and a half years to live.
options: He was gave two and a half years to live by the doctors.
He is given two and a half years to live by the doctors.
He was given two and a half years to live by the doctors.
questions.rule: Simple past passive with a person as subject: He was given ... (give - gave - given).

questions.source: Switch off your phones during the lecture.
options: Let your phones be switch off during the lecture.
Let your phones be switched off during the lecture.
Let your phones are switched off during the lecture.
questions.rule: Command in the passive: Let + object + be + past participle.

questions.source: My uncle started teaching physics in 2015. He still teaches it.
options: My uncle has taught physics for 2015.
My uncle has taught physics since 2015.
questions.rule: An action that began in the past and still goes on: present perfect + since + point in time.

questions.rule: Passive = be + past participle: was taken, was injected. Singular Hawking takes was.
